title: The French Revolution in 1789: A Connected Timeline
purpose: History fixture for chronology, map placement, primary-text evidence, multi-causal explanation, qualified interpretation, rights credits, and source-oriented review.

learner.audience: Secondary-school history learners studying causes, sequence, and historical interpretation.

objectives.statement: Place five major events of 1789 in chronological and geographic context.
criteria: Orders May, June, July, August, October

objectives.statement: Explain the Revolution as multi-causal rather than assigning one sole cause.
criteria: Names fiscal, institutional, social/economic, and intellectual factors

objectives.statement: Distinguish the Declaration's rights claims from unequal historical inclusion.
criteria: Does not equate universal wording with immediate universal participation

claims.statement: The sequence runs from the Estates-General in May through National Assembly, Bastille, Declaration, and the October march.
Fiscal, institutional, privilege/food-pressure, and intellectual factors interacted; no single factor is presented as the sole cause.
The Declaration articulated universal rights language while practical inclusion remained contested and unequal.

scenes.title: Paris and Versailles
scenes.narration: The story moves repeatedly between Versailles, the royal and assembly setting, and Paris, a center of popular action.
scenes.visualIntent: A restrained France inset and an Île-de-France detail label Paris and Versailles with shape markers and a scale note.
scenes.captionText: Two linked places: Versailles and Paris
scenes.accessibilityDescription: A map labels Versailles southwest of Paris and uses distinct marker shapes in addition to color.

scenes.title: Five turning points in 1789
scenes.narration: From May to October, political declarations, popular action, and institutional change unfolded in a connected sequence.
scenes.visualIntent: Five dated nodes use equal visual weight and connect to the map without implying inevitable progress.
scenes.accessibilityDescription: A five-item chronological list names each event and place.

scenes.title: Causes interact
scenes.narration: State debt, institutional conflict, unequal privilege, food pressure, and political ideas interacted. This is not a single-cause story.
scenes.visualIntent: A multi-node causal web uses bidirectional/context links and avoids one dominant root arrow.
scenes.accessibilityDescription: Five labeled factors connect in a network; the narration explains that the links are interacting pressures.

scenes.title: Rights language and historical limits
scenes.narration: The Declaration used universal rights language. That language and the unequal boundaries of participation must be examined together, not collapsed into one claim.
scenes.visualIntent: A locally typeset quotation-free document abstraction pairs textual principles with a clearly labeled historical-qualification panel.
scenes.captionText: Universal rights language ≠ immediate universal inclusion
scenes.accessibilityDescription: A two-column comparison distinguishes what the Declaration claimed from the limits of political participation.

scenes.title: Evidence and interpretation
scenes.narration: Review the Declaration text and the linked historical exhibition context, then keep factual chronology separate from interpretive explanation.
scenes.visualIntent: Credits list local note plus two external reviewer URIs; no remote image is embedded.
scenes.captionText: Sources: local teaching note • Constitutional Council • Library of Congress
scenes.accessibilityDescription: A source list gives titles and complete accessible links.

qualityAssertions.description: Event order and dates match the source note.
Narration and diagram never present one factor as sufficient or inevitable.
Every claim retains exact local support and external reviewer links.
Paris and Versailles are distinguishable without color and described in text.
The fixture embeds no remote or rights-unknown historical image.

provenance.notes: Local teaching note is the test source; official external links are reviewer context and never fetched by the fixture.
